item.title: Realistic Portal gun SCP idea
item.description: What would happen if a Portal Gun actually existed.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror, Drama/Emotional

Page Layout (Optional): Containment procedures, description, experimentation and recovery log

Elevator Pitch: There are many 'Portal' type anomalies in the SCP foundation, but never one that functions as a Gun. But what would happen if one existed.

Central Narrative: The anomaly is a stereotypical portal gun, that looks entirely like one from the game 'Portal' and functions as such. However, there are two twists to this concept:

+ Twists
- Close

1. Whenever someone makes a logical deduction about how a device would work, based on various aspects of science such as anti-matter or wormholes, the device will conform to that conclusion. For example, if a foundation scientist deduced that the edges of the portal would logically be superheated and produce large amounts of plasma, the portals will start doing so. The only exceptions to this are conclusions that would pre-empt the existence of the device or its initial functionality of shooting portals. These effects halt when the portal gun is deactivated. Eventually the foundation gets the bright idea to use the gun to create a generator, manned by uneducated D-Class, which ends in disaster when one realizes the portals violate the conservation of energy.

2. The device was recovered from a Level 2 reality bender. However this reality bender was also a quantum physicist and had built up an unshakable belief in the science, leading to the self-suppression of his abilities when they emerged. However the reality bender (hereafter called 'Bob') was also a fan of science fiction, especially the game 'Portal'. 'Bob' attended a sci-fi con with a model portal gun he had built himself and was discussion the possibility of making a real one in the future via use of quantum physics. Some of the other people at the con made fun of this, making him angry and temporarily un-suppressing his reality bending. Bob caused his portal to become 'real' and shot an actual portal, before realizing how such a thing wasn't possible. This lead to the anomaly in its current state. Bob was severely injured by the resulting extreme temperatures before the device was shut down by undercover agents at the sci-fi con. In hospital Bob writes a note about the clash between fiction and reality leading to his downfall before dying.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: A concept that would usually be placed in a -J article being presented seriously.

Additional Notes: I am unsure of the Creative Commons policy for game icons.

item.title: Be Careful What You Wish For
item.description: What more could a man who fears death ask for?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP article

Genre (Optional): Tragedy

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP article with tests logs, emails, and security footage.

Elevator Pitch: SCP is a laptop that contains images of how it's user will die. It's possible to avoid the death that the images show, but they will be replaced with the new eventual death of the user.(Example: A morbidly obese man may see images of himself dying of heart failure in a hospital. Exercising and losing weight would change his fate, and the images would show his death coming much later.) Too many subversions of the images will cause the user to enter a comatose state from which they cannot recover, and they cannot die. They are fully conscious in the coma, being able to see, hear, smell, feel, etc.

Central Narrative: Main narrative will follow a Junior Researcher fearing the death they see for themself. They become obsessed with avoiding death using the laptop and eventually go too far and have to face the consequences of never dying, but not really living. Test logs and emails will show their growing obsession with using the SCP to avoid death, and surveillance log will show how that obsession culminates in unauthorized access to the SCP.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Hinting at the fate of the Researcher in the description and containment procedures, and seeing how the relatable fear of death can push someone to act in a way that they know is wrong.

Additional Notes: I've struggled in the past with having a "story" in my ideas so I'm particularly interested if I'm more on track this time.

item.title: Collapsable side panel on all browser sizes
item.description: The navigation panel on the left side of the page should have a button to collapse it out of the way on the desktop/tablet version of the site
item.content:encoded:
Description: Wikidot uses adaptive scaling for its UI elements. There is a navigation panel on the left side of the site that, when the screen is less than 768 pixels1, collapses off screen with a button to bring it in and out. I request that this panel have be collapsible regardless of window size (although it would be open by default for medium-large screens). An example of this behavior can be found here.

If this is not possible, a simpler option would be to change the 768 breakpoint to a larger value. For this I conjecture that 1500 pixels would be approximately correct.

Reason: The side panel does not adapt well to tablet devices. When using a tablet device in portrait mode, the panel is stuck taking up about a third of the screen, while providing little value. This, in my opinion, dramatically harms the reading experience. This problem is easily remedied for all devices by making the panel collapsible.

In the event that this is not feasible, I suggest a breakpoint of 1500 pixels based on my knowledge of common device sizes. Once you step down from a desktop monitor, devices are almost exclusively tablets and smartphones2. On either of those devices, the panel should be hidden by default, regardless of their horizontal resolution. For this reason, I suggest a value that is only a little lower than the standard horizontal resolution on a modern device, while still allowing for some padding for DPI scaled devices, such as laptops. This solution has weird edge cases, and could easily cause problems for other device sizes, so I don't recommend it unless there is no better option.

Advantages:

  • Improved readability for tablet devices, and other large portrait screens (some desktop setups use a "sideways" monitor for reading).
  • More economical use of screen space

Disadvantages:

  • Slight increase in UI "clutter", as a new button would need to be added
  • Increases required clicks by 1 for some navigation tasks on some browsers
Footnotes
1. This is the breakpoint listed in the CSS. In practice, the value will change based on various scaling settings of the device, because nothing is ever simple.
2. When considering actual hardware resolution. Laptops considerably complicate this problem because they frequently use DPI scaling, making them appear lower resolution than they actually are. My 1080p laptop "looks" like it has a horizontal resolution of 1650 pixels, because of DPI scaling.

item.title: Sir Reginald
item.description: A SCP that possesses people, but is unknowingly an entity from another reality
item.content:encoded:

Genre: Action

Page Layout: Might include a journal written by the SCP later in the article's progression

Elevator Pitch: The SCP entity has the ability to passively possess any sentient beings within a certain radius upon the termination of the previous host. Upon possession, it will immediately overwrite the host's brain with the entity's personality. SCP-1 will also have an increase in intelligence/IQ scaling according to the intelligence of the host pre-possession (the smarter the host, the smarter SCP-1 is). SCP-1 is initially oblivious to the fact that they possesses people.

SCP-1 has an affinity to create advanced weapons. The dangerousness of the weapons also scale with the intelligence of the host. Due to this, the Foundation facilitates the containment of the entity by guaranteeing the termination of it’s previous host within suitable range of a “dumb” enough host. Foundation researchers theorize that given a smart enough host, SCP-1 could cause a XK-Class Scenario.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The SCP is actually a character from a fictional universe in the SCP universe, who somehow got into the base SCP universe through a reality anomaly. The entity has a confused memory of its life, and is missing many details about itself.

Someone working the Foundation comments on the similarities they saw between SCP-1 and a character in a show that they watched as a kid to SCP-1, the entity is confused by the character's name, aggressively claiming to not be/know the character. The SCP slowly regains a sense of self awareness throughout the article due to this, slowly regaining memories and gradually realizing what it is, going insane.

The Foundation also is looking into utilizing its intelligence increase potential on Foundation employees to help create anomalous weapons that would help the containment of other SCPs.

Hook: The premise of a SCP slowly losing its mind due to it being foreign to the universe and its rules.

item.title: The Normality
item.description: A person who's a living reality anchor.
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The most average man in the world, who's everything (height, weight, general routine, you name it) is very normal, has the unconscious power to remove the abnormal properties of every anomaly he comes across temporarily, if not erase it completely, provided that they should remain under his observable range or presence. Doesn't realize his powers, since every anomalous event is forcibly made to look normal to him.

Central Narrative: The Normality was found by accident when one of the SCP broke containment and coincidentally ran into him, henceforth being neutralized and re-secured. At first the foundation takes an interest in him, trying to recruit him since he could be a key to neutralizing all anomaly.

However, none of the foundation members were able to approach him due to his nature, and they decided instead to use him indirectly, by testing and putting forward SCPs to be erased. However, when they planned on erasing a keter class using him, it results in the foundation almost collapsing, since the foundation itself could be considered an anomaly, and anything that could affect his normal life gets influenced by his ability.

After closely preventing that, further testing and attempts to erase anomalies was stopped, because every anomaly he encounters afterwards carries the risk of letting the foundation come under his influence. Hence he was given SCP status, put under watch, and was prevented from coming in contact with anything abnormal.

Hooks: SCP is famous for trying to keep the most anomalous in check. It would interest both new and old fans to see how they would try to deal with the opposite. Also, the foundation's primary goal is to preserve reality and order. The normality could show an outlook on when moving towards that very goal can be disastrous.

Additional notes: This is my first SCP. Please tell me how may I improve on this, if any.

item.title: The Bone Seer
item.description: Can you hear the Song the bones sing?
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Mystery

Page Layout (Optional): Standard SCP document with a large focus on interview/experiment logs

Elevator Pitch: A woman capable of gaining information about others by handling their bones (as well as passing the information on) turns herself in to the Foundation, motivated by a steadfast belief that a K-class scenario is coming.

Central Narrative: After an unrelated incident in which an agent was KIA, the SCP, then working as a mortician, becomes aware of the Foundation via handling the agent's bones and shortly after turns itself in to the Foundation. After the Foundation ensures it's not a GOI agent, the SCP is taken in.

The SCP is able to gain information through physical contact with the bones of others (by what it claims is "listening to the Song") and carve the bones with various occult symbols to allow others to similarly glean the information. It claims its abilities are not born/naturally occurring but rather were taught to it by its grandmother. As the SCP has no living family, the info can not be verified. No attempts to recreate the scrimshaw by using the same symbols or teach others to "listen to the Song" have been successful.

+ show block
– hide block

The SCP is motivated by a zealous belief that a K-class scenario is coming soon, though it doesn't know when or how, and the details it describes do not match any known K-class scenarios. It's unclear whether the claim is valid or merely religious - possibly a side effect of the repeated use of its abilities, as it can sometimes have problems distinguishing its own memories from the ones gained via its abilities. This belief does however leave it completely cold and apathetic to individual lives, including its own, as well as highly cooperative with the Foundation, believing it will be necessary to try and piece the world together after the cataclysm.

The Foundation is left trying to find out how reliable is the SCP itself and its claims, as well the extent of its abilities to gain and pass information and whether it could be useful, though it remains wary of possible memetic agents.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The reader is left trying to figure out exactly how the SCP works and thinks, how sane it is, and can then turn to the experiment logs to see how various test subjects deal with having the memories of others, sometimes not even human.

It failed, but the SCP should be contained at a safer location. While in transport to that location, the SCP attacks his guards and walks away. Foundation personal see the SCP, but they aren't alarmed (the third bullet list point, remember?). The SCP walks into the lunch room of the scientific department, and murders senior researcher ''insert name here''. After that, the involved Foundation personal are given a class E status, but are cleared for duty after intensive mental and psychic tests.

Reason for my SCP to do that I hope this makes sense

Wouldn't it be terrible, not knowing what is real and what is fake? And when you have been fooled so many times that you thought you couldn't be fooled anymore, and then someone you started seeing as a friend betrays you? Well that is what my SCP was thinking. The researcher it murdered was a spy for the organization, as is later discovered by the Foundation (she was the one to try and murder the SCP). My SCP recognized the voice, and thought that it was all just some sort of organization test. It leaves a note saying: ''I believed you'', where he is talking to the junior researcher from bullet list point 4.

The organization
The idea is that there is an organization that tries to recreate gods/mythological creatures from the past trough genetic engineering. They try to create a leap-back in evolution, otherwise known as an atavism. Evolution is always positive, so reversing it should be mostly negative. That's why most of their attempts fail, or the creature dies at a young age. When the Foundation does an attack on one of its labs, they've already emptied it. Except for one: my SCP. They conduct, just like the Foundation, tests and contain the creatures safely.

What the Foundation is going to do next
Since the SCP is the only asset of information about the organization, it should be recovered as soon as possible, and not be killed. The Foundation found a series of text messages on the spy her laptop, talking about killing the SCP. The Foundation needs to find it, before they do.

Elevator Pitch: A man under the affect of a seeming "curse". Anyone who verbally confirms any relationship between them and the man dies within the next 24 hours in an unspeakably horrific way, varying from person to person.

Central Narrative: Man of None", a concept I had for an SCP, is a seemingly regular man with a personal love for technology. However, what is strange is the fact anyone who verbally recognizes a relationship between the speaker and the object are killed within 24 hours in an unspeakably painful way. While this may seem as if it's simply for the shock factor of gore and horrific deaths, there's a much darker thing behind it.

+ show block
– hide block

He wants to die, however due to the nature of the SCP Foundation his death would be something which would not be wanted. So, they contain him and give him psychological treatment (of course on a very strict regiment), however it never helps. With plenty of research, the only way which suicide patients are helped is via forming relationships with those who help them. And, any relationship with him causes horrific death. So, he's left alone in the world. All that people will call him is an object. They will not say he's their "friend". Not a "loved one". "Family", "enemy", any of the sort is never heard from them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The man, due to irrelevant trauma, has developed [REDACTED] disorder - which, with hints throughout the article, would be Borderline Personality Disorder. He is absolutely desperate for some form of recognition, approval, or relationship between another human. However, due to the nature of his "curse", he's unable to. This plays to one of the largest human fears of being truly alone. He, at first, tries to isolate himself from other people as to not harm them, however the more he isolates himself the more he becomes desperate to have confirmation in himself and social interaction. And when his greed takes over and he tries to reach out, the people he love die in a horrifically unspeakable way. Watching that is a trauma which most cannot imagine.

  • Small items may be offered as 'tribute' to prevent the doll's nature from taking important concepts/people. More complex concepts take longer to absorb.
  • Individuals under the effect may discuss subjective traits like beauty, coolness, etc. but may not discuss any precise details of the character beyond its displayed gender and that it is an anime figurine.
  • When asked, individuals under the effect will reflect questions such as 'YOU don't know HER?' 'I can't believe you'd have to ask me that; a REAL fan would know.' Which draws curiosity and a potential new victim.
  • The student discovered the figure and gradually became a classic case of neglecting himself in favor of the idol, gatekeeping while lording over them how great his new obsession was.

Central Narrative:

This story will be delivered in a series of interviews and found footage:

+ show block
– hide block

The doll was found in a college dorm closet whose occupant, a once sociable and incredibly bright young individual, began failing out due to offering term papers and other collegiate supplies. Initially thinking that the student was a hoarder, not much thought was given to the situation until the closet was forcefully cleaned and the student's roommate was found bound, malnourished, and near-death within the mass, assumed to be given as tribute when the student did not have anything else to give. Interrogation revealed that after running out of things to give the figure, the student began feeling a building pressure coming from the closet, adding to his overall stress levels as he began to notice a loss of personal identity nuance.

This discovery leads to him offering his roommate as tribute in a panic.

To remain generally inert, the item must receive a tribute every 2-3 days. However, a note from Foundation management has requested that office supplies no longer be offered due to the supply closet constantly needing to be restocked. The longer the doll goes without tribute, the stronger its pull.

Central Narrative: Taking place in august of 1965, just before SCP-1498 (which this tale is about) is contained, a troublesome teenager, Ty, stumbles across SCP-1498 in the woods and learns that he can order dreams from the SCP. He begins to abuse the ability, spending most of his time asleep, dreaming. However, when his body begins to slowly turn into instances of the SCP, he attempts to find "The Oneiroi Collective" (the people who possibly designed the SCP) to help him. However, upon searching phone books, he discovers that the phone number to call them only exists on the instances of SCP-1498. He hurries back to where he last saw them, but they've vanished completely. Luckily, a phone wire that goes through the woods leads him to an abandoned office building, where he finds the livestock entering. Ty catches up to them, managing to get on the phone with The Oneiroi Collective. However, it's too late, and Ty completely transforms into an instance of SCP-1498-1, mindlessly wandering back into the woods, ironically dreaming of the days when he didn't dream at all.

Anomalous instruction pamphlets designed to maim/kill seemingly random people across the globe… (all criticism welcome)

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Elevator Pitch: An anomalous set of pamphlets that compel the reader to do whatever the pamphlet has written on it- for example, if one said "read this pamphlet over and over", the subject would be forced to read the pamphlet over and over until it is taken from them or they expire.

Central Narrative: A group of researchers testing the capabilities of the SCP after MTF recovery units with memetic resistance find multiple pamphlets in seemingly random homes in urban areas such as Berlin, NYC, and London. Interviews with the owners of the homes show that they all have had attempts on their lives through anomalous means within the past three months.

+ show block
– hide block

The people are administered amnestics and are put back in their homes with a Foundation agent trailing them to make sure they are not killed. The researchers begin investigations on possible reasons why the makers of the pamphlets are targeting these people. One of the D-Class testing personnel notices that the contents of the pamphlet have changed.

The pamphlet writes about how the hitmen attempting to kill these people know that the Foundation has acquired the pamphlets and that the hitmen will not be so careless in the future, potentially setting up an opportunity for there to be more to the story.

The Foundation intercepts a radio transmission detailing the failure of the pamphlets, and discussing potential plans for the future. Foundation agents find a connection between the targets of the killings: they have all been involved in numerous black-market purchases of anomalous objects.

The Foundation discovers the existence of a group of assassins hired by existing groups to carry out their dirty work. The group has been implicated in over 260 murders, burglaries and other crimes across the globe, starting in 2008.

The article ends with all the pamphlets changing to contain the message WE’LL BE WATCHING. SIGNED WITH LOVE, [PLACEHOLDER NAME] (Still thinking of a name.)

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The different pamphlets have different instructions tailored to the individuals who received them. Each of them seems to be designed to seriously maim or kill the person who received them. The mystery of why these people are being targeted by anomalous killers is also a good hook.

Additional Notes: With this SCP, I am hoping to set up an opportunity for a new GOI or POI and more SCPs. I'm considering making this a tale instead, but I've always liked SCPs with a little more story meat on their bones. All criticism is appreciated!

Elevator Pitch: A tube of Petroleum jelly. When ointment is applied to a human, a person's hygiene is enhanced. Prominent symptom manifest in the form of pheromone secretion and irrational compulsion to spread the ointment. Hours after patient zero is infected, the infected encounter amorphous entities. Appearing entities embody subconscious fetishes or extremest fears. They ignore beings lacking pheromone and are hostile to those marked with pheromone.

Central Narrative: On the 9th December, the mysterious disappearance of 25 guests and staff at the Westhaven Luxury Lodge made national headlines. A team of four Field Agents stationed at Nelson, New Zealand take over the investigation and create a cover story.

Field Agents are briefed about the crime scene by the police. Exploring the lodge they find five rooms in the hallway cordoned off by police tape. Foundation agents are alarmed by the crude messages scratched into the Manuka wood and signs glued onto the walls left behind by the lodging's former occupants. Text advertise and revere "a conditioner sent by the gods". Most jarringly, the other remainder of the text read "The knavish resistance were enlightened, now they too relish the heaven-sent scent". Conditioner called "Te Horoi Pai" , translated to Xtreme Conditioner is discovered and placed in containment. All other copies found in the Lodging or within Police custody are confiscated and destroyed.

Testing is conducted, discovering the anomaly's psycho-contagious nature. It's speculated an unknown G.O.I is at hand. A nationwide sweep, extensively covering every hotel, motel and supermarket in New Zealand, yields negative results. A Mobile Taskforce (Called Bad Hair Day) is conceived to monitor the domestic supply chain for wild instances.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Mass disappearance is unheard-of in the 21st century, creating mystery. The anomaly takes place in New Zealand. Testing reveals the ultimate fate of the Lodging's residents. Furthermore, the G.O.I theory is a hypothesis, since Te Horoi Pai is the product name but there is no brand associated nor a manufacturer stated on the bottle. Therefore, the Foundation attempts to contain a contagious SCP with no identified point of origin; an analogy for viral outbreak clusters with no immediate causes.

Additional Notes: This is a submission for my first "canon" SCP, so any form of criticism is appreciated (Bluntness is 100% tolerated but please be constructive).
